translation: Youth swelling in my body, a young woman's charms on display
Youth swelling in my body, a young woman's charms on display
This wretched night, and the heat in my eyes all evening long
Whirling round, my pot broke into pieces
That young fellow's charm has ruined all my sleep
My heart is set on my young brother-in-law...
My feeble old husband, a worn-out screen whose luck has run out
My feeble old husband, a worn-out screen whose luck has run out
That monkey-face could not give me a son
That monkey-face could not give me a son
My crafty old husband dyed his moustache
My crafty old husband dyed his moustache
Tricked me, married me and brought me home
Oh my fate... this dark one... that fate of mine... oh, my fate...
He kept me away from my brother-in-law and laid his hidden snares
He brought me lots of jewellery and piled it on me from head to toe
He kept me away from my brother-in-law and laid his hidden snares
He brought me lots of jewellery and piled it on me from head to toe
When Dasara came, saying I had none... he put armlets on me
For Nagula Chavithi, to make me look lovely, he bought a gold necklace
For Karthika Purnima, calling me his new wife, he brought a gold-coin necklace
For Kanuma at Sankranti, he had gold plaque necklaces made for me
Hey, he says he'll gobble up the new bride he brought home
Hey, he says he'll gobble up the new bride he brought home
Afraid I'll run away... that I'll run off, he keeps following me around on guard
He keeps following me around on guard...
With this useless old screen, married life can't go on any more
We grabbed each other round and round and cursed each other, sister... cursed each other, sister...
Never mind the cursing,
we came to blows, O mother Nukamma, mother Nukamma
Caught in between the two of us, what punches flew, sister... what punches flew, sister...
Never mind all those punches,
we took a beating, O mother Nukamma, mother Nukamma
summaryEn:
"Vayasu Pongu" (The Swell of Youth) is a comic song from the album Telugu Folk Songs (2003), sung by A. Anasuya Devi, V. Seetha Devi and T.R. Jayadev. It is a satirical complaint by a young wife who has been married off to an old man, a mismatched marriage that folk songs often mock.

The young woman describes her restless youth and sleepless nights, and admits that her heart is drawn to her young brother-in-law. She pours scorn on her husband: he is feeble and past his prime, a "monkey-face" who could not give her a son, and a trickster who dyed his moustache to fool her into marrying him. To keep her away from the brother-in-law he showers her with jewellery at every festival: armlets at Dasara, a gold necklace for Nagula Chavithi, a coin necklace (kasula peru) at Karthika Purnima and plaque necklaces for Kanuma during Sankranti. Yet he is so jealous that he follows her everywhere, afraid she will run away. The song ends in slapstick, as she tells how the quarrel turned from curses to blows, calling on the village goddess Nukamma. The dialect words and forms of address such as "appo" give it an earthy, rustic flavour.
summaryTe:
"వయసు పొంగు" ఒక హాస్య, వ్యంగ్య గీతం. ఇది 2003 నాటి Telugu Folk Songs ఆల్బమ్‌లోనిది. దీన్ని ఎ. అనసూయ దేవి, వి. సీతాదేవి, టి.ఆర్. జయదేవ్ పాడారు. ముసలివాడికిచ్చి పెళ్ళి చేసిన ఒక పడుచు భార్య వెళ్ళగక్కే ఎగతాళి నిండిన ఫిర్యాదు ఇది. ఇలాంటి జోడు కుదరని పెళ్ళిళ్ళను జానపద పాటలు తరచూ వెక్కిరిస్తాయి.

ఆ పడుచు తన పొంగే వయసును, నిద్రపట్టని రాత్రులను వర్ణిస్తుంది. తన మనసు మరిది మీద ఉందని ఒప్పుకుంటుంది. మొగుడిని ఏకిపారేస్తుంది: పసలేని ముసలివాడు, దశ మళ్ళిన తడక, కొడుకును కూడా కనలేని కోతి మొగం, మీసాలకు రంగేసి మోసం చేసి పెళ్ళాడిన దోసకారి అంటుంది. ఆమెను మరిదికి దూరం చేయడానికి అతను ప్రతి పండుగకూ నగలు తెస్తాడు: దసరాకు దండ కడియాలు, నాగుల చవితికి నాను పేట, కార్తీక పున్నమికి కాసుల పేరు, సంక్రాంతి కనుమకు బంగారు పలక సరులు. అయినా అతనికి అనుమానం ఎక్కువ. ఆమె లేచిపోతుందేమోనని ఎక్కడికి వెళ్ళినా కాపలా కాస్తూ వెంట తిరుగుతాడు. చివరికి గొడవ తిట్లు దాటి కొట్లాట దాకా వెళ్ళిందని ఆమె గ్రామదేవత నూకమ్మను తలచుకుంటూ నవ్వు పుట్టేలా చెబుతుంది. యాస మాటలు, "అప్పో" లాంటి పిలుపులు పాటకు మట్టి వాసన ఉన్న పల్లె రుచిని ఇస్తాయి.
